**Title (English, from literature):** Eating ungiven food

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 40, titled *Dantapona* ("Eating ungiven food"), establishes the training rule that a monk who consumes food or drink that has not been formally offered must confess the offense. In modern discussion of the Vinaya, this rule prohibiting the consumption of unoffered food has been cited to illustrate how rules originally meant to prevent improper behavior (such as plucking fruit from an orchard without permission) can evolve into formal monastic rituals [Dhammika]. An English translation of the rule and its analysis has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
